subject: 199944841572430A878E76F5DDAC07BD
introduction: “Although divorce is permissible, yet it is strongly abhorred.” Bahá’í law allows divorce where aversion has become irremediable, and surrounds it with a year of patience in which reconciliation is to be attempted and support continued. The readings give the principle, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s explanations to individuals, some procedural rulings, and his comparison with the Gospel, which forbids divorce. The three earlier laws stand beside it: Deuteronomy’s bill of divorcement, given by the husband alone; Jesus’s “let not man put asunder”, and his explanation of Moses’s concession; and the Qur’an’s “retained in honour or released in kindness”, with its arbiters from both families.
questions: The Gospel forbids divorce; the Qur’an and the readings permit it reluctantly. What does each fear most?
What is the year of patience for? What would be lost without it?
Deuteronomy gives the initiative to the husband. How do readings 6 and 16 differ?
“Abhorred” yet “permissible”: how should a community treat those who divorce?

outside.why: Permissible, yet strongly abhorred. The Lord, the God of Israel, saith that he hateth putting away.
Jesus, asked whether a man may put away his wife: what therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder.
Where no harmony can be had, separation. A woman must be retained in honour or released in kindness.
Not to leave the wife without support. On the settlement at divorce the Qur’an adds: forget not kindness among yourselves.
Where it is impossible to recreate their love. Paul: if she depart, let her remain unmarried or be reconciled to her husband.

Aversion between husband and wife: the readings name both. The Mosaic law spoke of one side only: if she find no favour in his eyes, let him write her a bill of divorcement, and send her out of his house. What has changed between that law and reading 16?
The intention announced, and a year of waiting. Appoint an arbiter from his folk and an arbiter from her folk; if they desire amendment Allah will make them of one mind.
Bide in patience through one whole year. Charity suffereth long, and is kind; beareth all things, hopeth all things.
A year’s separation in hope of reunion. First be reconciled to thy brother, and then come and offer thy gift.
Souls quickened by the spirit avoided divorce altogether. It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.
Marriage and divorce carried out with the knowledge of those in authority. Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers.
Equal rights of men and women in divorce. There is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus.
“According to the explicit text of the Gospel, divorce is forbidden.” Moses because of the hardness of your hearts suffered you to put away your wives: but from the beginning it was not so.

shortfall: Readings 5, 7, 9, 10 and 11 repeat the ground of divorce or are rulings on witnesses, waiting periods and particular cases, for which nothing outside was sought.

malachi-he-hateth-putting-away.text: For the Lord, the God of Israel, saith that he hateth putting away

corinthians-let-not-the-wife-depart.text: And unto the married I command, yet not I, but the Lord, Let not the wife depart from her husband: But and if she depart, let her remain unmarried or be reconciled to her husband: and let not the husband put away his wife

deuteronomy-bill-of-divorcement.text: When a man hath taken a wife, and married her, and it come to pass that she find no favour in his eyes, because he hath found some uncleanness in her: then let him write her a bill of divorcement, and give it in her hand, and send her out of his house

quran-appoint-an-arbiter.text: And if ye fear a breach between them twain (the man and wife), appoint an arbiter from his folk and an arbiter from her folk. If they desire amendment Allah will make them of one mind. Lo! Allah is ever Knower, Aware.
